title: assert_scene_tracks_physics: cross-cutting scene ↔ physics coherence assertion
description:
The 'looks fine, isn't' bug class: a viewport can display a plausible scene while physics has diverged (a body slept off-screen, a body drifted, transforms went stale). Rapier and Scene3d each have honest state; nothing today checks they AGREE.

## API
Mob.Scene3d.Test.assert_scene_tracks_physics(scene_ir, transforms_fn, tolerance \\ 1.0e-3)
where transforms_fn returns [{entity_id, {x, y, z}, {qx, qy, qz, qw}}] - shape-compatible with RapierLab.Physics.transforms/1 return type and any future mob_rapier equivalent.

For each entity id present in BOTH the scene IR and the transforms list, assert position + rotation agree within tolerance. Physics-only entities (no scene mirror) are noted, not failed. Scene-only entities (camera, light, static ground) are ignored.

## Rationale
Kept physics-engine-agnostic - takes a function or plain list, doesn't depend on RapierLab or a specific mob_* plugin. Same helper covers dice, shells, cloth, whatever comes next.

## Acceptance
- ExUnit-style: raises on mismatch with a diff showing entity_id, expected, actual, delta
- Works from host over dist when the scene IR + transforms come from an RPC
- Guide entry in guides/agents.md as the top of the 'scene truth' section
- Test in test/mob/scene3d_assert_tracks_physics_test.exs including a passing case + a failing case with expected error message
- CHANGELOG entry
close_reason: SHIPPED on worktree agent-readback (commit 91ad97d): Mob.Scene3d.Test.Physics.assert_scene_tracks_physics/3 + MismatchError. Physics-engine-agnostic - takes {entity_id, {x,y,z}, {qx,qy,qz,qw}} shape that RapierLab.Physics.transforms/1 already returns. Handles quat sign ambiguity, list-shaped JSON readback, custom tolerance, phantom-body noting. 9 new tests, full suite 164/164.

title: Agent-friendly readback: entity_aabb(vp, entity_id) -> world-space AABB
description:
Filament's TransformManager and RenderableManager already know each entity's world-space AABB per-frame. Exposing it makes agent-side visibility + framing tests trivial: given the AABB and the camera you can compute the on-screen rect for the entity or ask 'is the whole entity in the view frustum'.

## API
Mob.Scene3d.entity_aabb(node, viewport_id, entity_id) - host.
Mob.Scene3d.entity_aabb(viewport_id, entity_id, timeout) - device-local.
Returns {:ok, %{min: {x, y, z}, max: {x, y, z}}} or {:error, {:no_entity, id}} or {:error, {:no_viewport, id}}.

## Native surface
nif_scene3d_entity_aabb(vp, req_id, %{entity_id}) enqueues on render thread. iOS: iterate Renderable instances under the entity's TransformManager subtree; take the union of their world-space AABBs. Android: same via RenderableManager JNI.

## Acceptance
- Runs on iOS + Android
- Entity without renderables (camera, light) returns 0-sized AABB at the entity origin - honest, not an error
- Entity with children unions children's AABBs
- Guide entry in guides/agents.md paired with project/1 as the pair 'find and measure entity in the frame'
- Test in test/mob/scene3d_entity_aabb_test.exs
- CHANGELOG entry

title: Agent-friendly readback: project(vp, entity_id) -> screen-space {x, y, depth, in_frame?}
description:
Companion to sample_region + pick. Given a viewport id and entity id, return the entity origin projected into the viewport's pixel space using the CURRENT camera. Lets agents answer 'is entity X visible and where?' without doing projection math. Combined with sample_region({x - w/2, y - h/2, w, h}) an agent can verify 'the pixels where entity X should be actually show it'.

## API
Mob.Scene3d.project(node, viewport_id, entity_id) - host-side.
Mob.Scene3d.project(viewport_id, entity_id, timeout) - device-local, default timeout 5000ms.
Returns {:ok, %{x, y, depth, in_frame?}} or {:error, {:no_entity, id}} or {:error, {:no_viewport, id}}.

## Native surface
nif_scene3d_project(vp, req_id, %{entity_id}) enqueues on render thread. Renderer reads TransformManager world_transform for the entity, multiplies by camera view/projection, converts NDC to pixel using current viewport size, replies via s3d_reply.

## Acceptance
- Runs on iOS + Android
- Returns pixel {x, y} inside viewport bounds when entity center is on-screen; in_frame? mirrors that
- Off-frame entities still return coords with in_frame?=false so agents can reframe
- depth as NDC z distinguishes 'behind camera' from 'ahead'
- Guide entry in guides/agents.md pairing project + sample_region + pick as the readback triple
- Test in test/mob/scene3d_project_test.exs
- CHANGELOG entry
close_reason:
project/N landed as an Elixir-side computation off scene()'s existing world_transform readback — same authoritative Filament TransformManager source the render thread uses, no new NIF surface, one-file diff.

Matrix math split into Mob.Scene3d.Projection (perspective/4, inverse/1, mul_vec/2, ndc_to_pixel/3, project_entity/6) so the hot pieces are testable as pure functions. Facade in Mob.Scene3d.project/N mirrors pick's overload pattern (host/device shapes, default viewport).

viewport_size arrives as {w, h} in dp/pt from the caller — the same values the screen declared with Mob.Scene3d.viewport(...). A future NIF revision that reads _view->getViewport() natively can drop that argument; the facade shape stays the same either way. Noted the design tradeoff in the docstring + CHANGELOG so a follow-up bead can push project() to the render thread if animated scenes that mutate transforms outside the IR flow ever need real-time authoritative answers.

Guide entry (guides/agents.md) writes up the pick + project + sample_region readback triple with a runnable example. Registered in ex_doc's :extras.

Host tests: 18 new (scene3d_projection_test.exs — pure math; scene3d_project_test.exs — facade with a mocked Native impl, error paths for missing entity / camera / bad scene). Full mob_scene3d suite 173/173.

Moto G verify (through rapier_lab, which path-deps mob_scene3d):
  - camera projects to (186, 250) = viewport center — expected (camera-through-its-own-view = origin at NDC 0,0)
  - ground origin projects to (186, 411) — center-x, lower half; camera pitched down at -40° from y=0.9 looks down at the floor, so the origin lands below the horizon line. Matches the mental picture.
  - shell_4 (still inside arena, at world (-0.088, 0.010, -0.292)) projects to (162, 302) — slightly left of centre, below the horizon. Matches world position.
  - project → sample_region(x - 16, y - 16, 32, 32) → dominant colour readback closes the triple end-to-end.
  - Error paths honest: {:error, {:no_entity, id}} for a missing entity id.

Follow-ups surfaced:
  - Native-authoritative variant (single-tick NIF that reads TransformManager on the render thread instead of via scene readback). File a bd when a real animated scene needs it.
  - rapier_lab arena leak: 6 of 7 shells escaped the arena walls (positions 1+ metres from origin, arena_half=0.20). Not a mob_scene3d issue but flagged for the shells demo — probably wall thickness/damping.
  - Scaled cameras: general 4x4 inverse handles them, but face-camera scenes should stay rigid. No known caller uses a scaled camera.
